rv.q: Ill served by the production, Frances Poet’s adaptation also suffers from inert discussion and explanatory scenes that interrupt the drama’s forward movement.
As it is, it feels as though there is a bolder, brasher, better production struggling to get out.
If the tone of Poet and Nichols’ show more resembles Elinor than Marianne, in terms of its romantic rites of passage, it nevertheless remains a merry dance of a show.

cn.t: Critics are split on this Austen adaptation: its pop-song soundtrack and modern irreverence win some over, but others find it falls short of its fun premise. Solid staging, uneven execution.
